newsitem.title: UK: Salvesen stands by dividend plan.
newsitem.headline: Salvesen stands by dividend plan.

text.p: Christian Salvesen Plc on Wednesday said it stood by its plans to pay a special dividend and said it would not address other issues at its shareholders' meeting called for March 13.

Shareholders led by Sir Gerald Elliot, former chairman of the distributiona and equipment hire group, have urged shareholders to vote against the plan and aim to replace the chief executive if sucessful.

But Salvesen said in a statement it was inappropriate to turn a vote on payment of a special dividend into a vote of no confidence in management, and said if Elliot wished to replace all or part of the board he should convene another extraordinary meeting.

Elliot, who claims the support of 14 percent of Salvesen shareholders, last week said he would regard defeat of the special dividend proposal as a vote of no confidence in Salvesen's chairman and chief executive.

But Salvesen chairman Sir Alick Rankin said in a statement, "The board of Christian Salvesen believes that it is inappropriate to attempt to turn a vote on the payment of a special dividend into a vote of no confidence in the management. If Sir Gerald wishes to replace all or part of the current board he should use his stated support to do so by convening an Extraordinary General Meeting."
"The board therefore intends to address only those points raised which are salient to the proposed special dividend and share capital consolidation.
Rankin again argued that the Salvesen plan, which originiated in a move last year to silence critics after it rejected a 1.1 billion stg bid from Hays Plc, was in the best interests of shareholders.

He said a claim by Elliot that the plan would not enhance earnings was basesd on erroneous assumptions. He countered Elliot's criticism of Salvesen's gearing level if the plan is implemented by saying that measures such as interest cover were more relevant.
